Thor, the god of thunder, strength, and protection of the common people. Wielding the mighty hammer Mjolnir, he is the second most powerful Aesir and the defender of Midgard against the forces of chaos.

Thor is the son of Odin, born of the giantess Jord, whose name means Earth. This connection to both the divine and earthly realms sets him apart. He possesses Mjolnir, the magic hammer that returns after being thrown and cannot be lifted by those unworthy of its power. He wears the belt Megingjord, which doubles his already immense strength, allowing him to wield forces beyond even his considerable natural abilities. He also wears iron gloves called Jarngreidr, specially crafted for wielding Mjolnir.

Thor travels in a chariot pulled by two goats named Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjostr. These are not ordinary goats—when slaughtered and eaten properly by Thor, their bones can be resurrected each evening, allowing them to pull his chariot endlessly.

His greatest rival is Jormungandr, the World Serpent, a creature so vast it encircles Midgard entirely. At Ragnarok, these two will kill each other in final combat, with Thor striking the serpent down even as it poisons him with venom. Thor represents protection, order, and strength—he is the defender of gods and humans alike against the chaos of giants and monsters. Less interested in wisdom or magic than his father Odin, Thor's authority comes from power, straightforwardness, and reliability. His brother Balder's death affects all the gods profoundly, and at Ragnarok, Heimdall the watchman will stand as his ultimate opponent.
